- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥1.0) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) in recent history, model underestimates prices; increase forecast lows by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 3–7 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in medium-term (15–30d) forecasts; if forecast is >10% above recent 10d average, adjust downward by 2–5%.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, model fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast upward by 3–8% in the first 5 days of the new sentiment trend.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >15% in 3 consecutive days, apply a “reversion penalty” — reduce next forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
